title: Stable models by hand
description: The answer sets of a disjunctive logic program given as facts; deciding whether one exists is Sigma-2-complete (Eiter and Gottlob). The abstraction guesses a classical model of the rules, the check looks for a smaller model of the reduct, and relevant/1 names the atoms that make this smaller model work. The sample program is itself a guess-and-saturate encoding of an exists-forall formula.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The object program, as facts. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% A disjunctive logic program, as facts. head(R,A): atom A is in the head of rule R;
% pos(R,A): A is in the body; neg(R,A): "not A" is in the body.
% The program guesses p, q and r and then tests them by saturation:
%  1: p :- not np.          2: np :- not p.
%  3: q :- not nq.          4: nq :- not q.
%  5: r :- not nr.          6: nr :- not r.
head(1,p). neg(1,np).       head(2,np). neg(2,p).
head(3,q). neg(3,nq).       head(4,nq). neg(4,q).
head(5,r). neg(5,nr).       head(6,nr). neg(6,r).
%  7: a ; b.      8: c ; d.      9: e ; f.
head(7,a). head(7,b).       head(8,c). head(8,d).       head(9,e). head(9,f).
% 10: w :- a, c, p.        11: w :- a, c, r.
% 12: w :- a, d.           13: w :- b, c, e, q.
% 14: w :- b, c, f.        15: w :- b, d.
head(10,w). pos(10,a). pos(10,c). pos(10,p).
head(11,w). pos(11,a). pos(11,c). pos(11,r).
head(12,w). pos(12,a). pos(12,d).
head(13,w). pos(13,b). pos(13,c). pos(13,e). pos(13,q).
head(14,w). pos(14,b). pos(14,c). pos(14,f).
head(15,w). pos(15,b). pos(15,d).
% 16..21: a :- w.  b :- w.  c :- w.  d :- w.  e :- w.  f :- w.
head(16,a). head(17,b). head(18,c). head(19,d). head(20,e). head(21,f).
pos(16..21,w).
% 22: :- not w.
rule(22). neg(22,w).
rule(R) :- head(R,_).
atom(A) :- head(_,A).
atom(A) :- pos(_,A).
atom(A) :- neg(_,A).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): classical models of the program.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of atoms that satisfies every rule read as a classical implication
% (if the body holds, an atom of the head is true).
{ in(A) } :- atom(A).
:- rule(R), in(A) : pos(R,A); not in(A) : neg(R,A); not in(A) : head(R,A).
#show in/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the atoms of the candidate model.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a smaller model of the reduct (solver C).
fragments.text:
% The reduct with respect to the candidate drops every rule with "not A" in its body
% for an atom A of the candidate, and the negative literals of the other rules.
gone(R) :- neg(R,A), in(A).
% A counterexample: a proper subset of the candidate that satisfies the reduct.
% Then the candidate is not a minimal model of its reduct, so it is not stable.
{ sub(A) } :- in(A).
:- rule(R), not gone(R), sub(A) : pos(R,A); not sub(A) : head(R,A).
left(A) :- in(A), not sub(A).
smaller :- left(A).
:- not smaller.
#show sub/1.

% What the counterexample depends on:
% - its own atoms stay in the candidate;
relevant(in(A)) :- sub(A).
% - one atom that it leaves out stays in the candidate too (the first one will do);
relevant(in(A)) :- left(A), not left(B) : atom(B), B < A.
% - a rule that the subset violates must stay out of the reduct: for each such rule,
%   the atoms that removed it stay in the candidate.
needed(R) :- gone(R), sub(A) : pos(R,A); not sub(A) : head(R,A).
relevant(in(A)) :- needed(R), neg(R,A), in(A).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
